data.one_liner: Manage and retrieve photo, video, and audio assets on Android, iOS, macOS, and OpenHarmony.
data.what_it_does: Provides low-level APIs to access, query, filter, and manage device media albums and files without built-in UI components. Supports requesting permissions, handling limited access, modifying asset metadata, and watching for library changes.
use_when: You need to build a custom media picker or gallery browser from scratch.
You require fine-grained programmatic control over device photo and video libraries.
avoid_when: You just want a ready-made picker UI without writing custom views.
You only need to pick a single image or file and can rely on higher-level drop-in pickers.
strengths: Extensive support for albums, custom filters, pagination, and file caching.
Cross-platform support covering Android, iOS, macOS, and OpenHarmony.
Active maintenance with advanced features like Live Photos, adjustments, and cloud identifiers.
weaknesses: Requires manual configuration of native platform permissions and dependencies.
Does not include any ready-to-use UI widgets for displaying or selecting media out of the box.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding platform permissions (NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription for iOS/macOS) and configuring minimum Android/Gradle/Kotlin versions.

alternatives.name: image_picker
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick images and videos quickly using the platform's native picker UI with minimal configuration.
